label: FY2027 Q2 (May–Jul 2026)
asOf: prices as of the 27 Oct 2026 close
headline: More orders than it can fill, but higher memory prices are eating gross margin first

points.t: Revenue +106%, a fourth straight quarter of acceleration; a preliminary view of about 70% more growth in FY28.
Memory prices rose more than expected; Q4 gross margin falls to 71–72%, and FY28 is only 72–73%.
Days sales outstanding 45 → 60, supply commitments doubled to $279B, and operating cash flow halved quarter on quarter.

reaction: Stock: closed −1.6% ($209.66) on report day, fell then rose after hours, and closed +8.7% ($227.98) the next day, its biggest one-day gain since April 2025; it gave back 4.6% on the third day. The rally came from Q3 guidance and the preliminary ~70% FY28 growth view, both well above expectations; the worries were gross margin guidance and $108.5B of guarantee exposure. It closed at $217.94 on 27 Oct, 4.4% below the day after the report. Expectations are publicly reported consensus (Yahoo Finance); from FY27, non-GAAP EPS includes stock-based compensation.

segments.title: By market
segments.take: Growth came almost entirely from data center, split evenly between two customer groups: large cloud providers doubled, and AI clouds, sovereign and enterprise customers grew faster still.

rows.why: Includes AI clouds such as CoreWeave, sovereign AI and enterprise customers, plus AI cloud compute rented by large cloud providers. Management says this will be about half of data center and grow faster than Hyperscale long term.
Public clouds and large internet companies, driven mainly by Blackwell Ultra. The small chart shows total data center revenue (Hyperscale + ACIE).
Gaming and PCs, workstations, automotive and robotics. Workstations sold well; consumer PCs were held back by higher memory and system prices.

segments.note: From FY27 NVIDIA reports data center and edge computing, with data center split into Hyperscale and ACIE. One customer moved from ACIE to Hyperscale after changing its business model, and prior quarters were restated. China Hopper shipments were under 1% of data center revenue.

extras.title: Why gross margin falls
extras.take: This quarter's 75% is the peak; the next two quarters head lower, mainly because of costs.

items.w: Management said memory price increases were “higher than we had previously expected”, the main reason Q4 gross margin falls to 71–72%.
Volume shipments began in August, about 20% of Q3 data center revenue. New products cost more early in the ramp.
Price increases already made take effect from FY28 Q1, so the FY28 gross margin guide returns to 72–73%.

extras.title: Cash comes back slower
extras.take: Revenue is rising, but cash is tied up in receivables, inventory and long-term purchase commitments.

items.w: Receivables of $63.1B. Payment terms were extended on multi-quarter contracts for some investment-grade large customers; last quarter it said DSO would return to about 55.
Built ahead for the Q3 Vera Rubin launch.
Up $160B in one quarter, mainly to lock in memory. $92B falls due this fiscal year and about $87–88B in each of FY28 and FY29.
Guarantees for partners' data-center land, power and buildings, including up to $105B for SB Energy. Payment is only needed if the counterparty defaults.

trends.why: Fourth straight quarter of acceleration; Q3 guided at $108B
75% is the peak; Q4 guided at 71–72%
GAAP includes $7.8B of investment gains; non-GAAP is $2.22
Halved q/q in Q2 as receivables and taxes rose

valuation.take: About 28x trailing earnings, the second lowest in its own five years. Even in the bear case (FY28 revenue up only 35%), the P/E is only about 20x: the market is discounting the risk that the AI investment cycle peaks, not paying a premium for next year's growth.

forward.title: Next quarter's earnings from company guidance
steps: Q3 revenue at the guided midpoint of $108.0B, 74% gross margin → gross profit about $79.9B
Less about $9.0B of non-GAAP operating expenses → operating income about $70.9B (66% margin)
Non-operating income at last quarter's $0.3B, 16% tax → net income about $59.8B
÷ 24.285B shares → Q3 EPS about $2.46 (pre-report public consensus about $2.38)
forward.note: The company gives no Q4 revenue guidance, so this only goes to Q3. Our estimate, not a company forecast.

scenarios.title: Three scenarios: where the price sits
head: Case
Revenue growth
Margin
EPS
P/E
scenarios.note: Margin is the operating margin; the base case follows management's “about 70% FY28 growth” and 72–73% gross margin. FY27 revenue is Q1 and Q2 actuals plus the Q3 guided midpoint, with Q4 assumed 8% above Q3, about $402B in total; 16% tax, 24.3B shares, excluding investment gains. *Price: if the market pays the five-year median forward P/E of 35x, the current price needs FY28 EPS of only $6.18, which at a 64% margin means revenue about 31% below FY27. The price sits below even the most pessimistic of the three scenarios. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

history.title: Against its own last 5 years
history.note: About 28x now, above only 1 of the last 20 quarter ends (26x at the end of July 2026), the 5th percentile; median about 52x. The 100x+ stretch in 2023 came from the stock rising before profits did, not from more confidence then. StockAnalysis data; quarter ends are NVIDIA's fiscal quarter ends (end of January, April, July, October).

decomp.title: The +8.7% post-report move, decomposed
head: Measure
TTM earnings
P/E
decomp.note: The new quarter replaces the one a year ago, so trailing EPS rose from $6.53 to $7.91. The stock rose less than earnings, and the multiple fell from 32x to 29x: the market accepted higher earnings but didn't pay more for them.

cash.title: Cash comes back slower
cash.note: Q2 operating cash flow was $24.1B, less than half of Q1's $50.3B, which the company attributed to working capital and higher taxes. Capex is small ($2.7B in Q2), so free cash flow depends mainly on receivables and inventory. Quarter-end cash and marketable securities were $56.6B, and $25B of new bonds were issued this quarter.

changes.now: Q3 74%, Q4 bottoming at 71–72%, FY28 72–73%; memory prices rose more than expected.

changes.before: Confident of $1T of Blackwell and Rubin revenue over 2025–2027.
changes.now: No longer cites $1T; instead a preliminary view of about 70% FY28 revenue growth, stressing supply limits and that true demand “would be much higher”.

changes.before: Mainly investments in AI labs and supply lock-ins.
changes.now: Working with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to bring in more than $500B of third-party capital; revenue backstops for some AI clouds, and guarantees of up to $108.5B.
NVIDIA's revenue opportunity per gigawatt of data center: about $18B for Hopper, about $25B for Blackwell and about $40B for Vera Rubin.

items: Top five customers' capex is close to $800B in 2026 and $1.3T in 2027
Expanded partnership with Amazon: another 2M GPUs by FY29 Q2
Vera Rubin has orders from every major cloud, AI cloud and system maker and will be the fastest ramp in company history
Grace CPU revenue exceeded $5B over the past four quarters; data center CPU revenue more than doubles in FY28

insider.title: Effective trades 30 days around the report
insider.text: No effective trades in the 30 days before the report (7/27–8/26). In the 30 days after: director Mark Stevens sold three times in the open market, about 4.24M shares for $947M (average about $223), outside any 10b5-1 plan. CFO Colette Kress and General Counsel Timothy Teter sold about $21M in total under planned sales, which we don't count as effective sales. No insider bought. Data from April's Stock Atlas insider activity.
